# ces-revisions roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-chatgpt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-claude.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-gemini.md.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | How the size of the one-month revision moves with the number of collection days before first release | A | 1 | Release calendar and monthly vintages: a day or two to assemble. Fit time: measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | How much of the one- and two-month revisions comes from late sample reports, and how much from seasonal-factor revision | A | 2 | Needs NSA and SA vintages together. Fit time: Stage 1's measurement sets the basis |
| O2 | How the size of the two-month revision moves with the first-closing collection rate | A | 3 | Collection-rate series: availability not yet checked. Fit time: Stage 1's measurement sets the basis |
| O6 | How revision size moves with CES sample size and sample attrition | B | 1 | Several days to hand-build from archived releases. Fit time: measured by Stage 2 |
| O4 | How revision size moves with real BLS appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdowns | B | 2 | Several days to hand-build from budget justifications |
| O5 | How revision size moves with BLS staffing counts | B | 3 | Several days to hand-build from budget justifications and staffing reports |

Tracks: A — collection interval and revision size (research). B — budget, staffing and sample (research). B is split from A because A rests on sharp month-to-month calendar variation that public release dates give directly. B's covariates move slowly, trend together and must be hand-built. Its answer does not change A's model.
Track ranking: A, then B.

## Stages
